insight: Cape Verde's performance in the 2026 World Cup shows a notable trend when it comes to hydration breaks, with the team gaining momentum in 7 out of 8 breaks, indicating a slight increase in their pace of play after the brief pause. This suggests that the breaks allow Cape Verde to regroup and refocus, leading to a more energetic and dynamic performance on the field. When Cape Verde was pressing before a hydration break, they tended to struggle to maintain their momentum, but when they weren't pressing, they were able to capitalize on the break and come out stronger, with a higher average increase in momentum. Overall, the data implies that hydration breaks have a positive impact on Cape Verde's gameplay, particularly when they're not exerting high pressure before the break, allowing them to recharge and gain an edge over their opponents.
